title: Week 2: The Heatwave

theme.name: Heatwave
theme.text: It's thirty-eight degrees. Fans, ice lollies and Big Carl on full alert. The Treasury melts a little every few cards.

cards.text: Boss. It's my birthday. I'm forty. In raccoon years that's three. I'd like a party. In the bins. The good bins. Can I?

right.label: Yes, a party
right.reaction: Thank you, boss. I've already invited everyone. Everyone is raccoons.

left.label: No party
left.reaction: That's fine. I'll just sit in a bin. On my birthday. Alone. With my thoughts.

cards.text: Randy's party has four hundred raccoons in it. They've formed a conga line. It goes through the bank. And out the vault. Shut it down?

right.label: Yes, shut it down
right.reaction: The conga line has stopped. It's still standing in the vault. Swaying. Waiting.

left.label: No, let them conga
left.reaction: The conga reached the next town. Their mayor joined. He's eaten a bin. He seems happier.

cards.text: Randy has been sitting in a bin for nine hours. Children are leaving him cake. Bev left a scone. The town feels terrible. Throw him a party?

right.label: Fine. Surprise party.
right.reaction: He cried so hard the bin lid closed. He's opened it again. He's still crying. Happily.

left.label: No. He's fine.
left.reaction: Marge has photographed him. 'DEPUTY SPENDS BIRTHDAY IN BIN.' Front page. In colour.

cards.text: Boss. My birthday cake's arrived. It's shaped like a bin. It IS a bin. Full of cake. The bill's enormous. Pay it?

right.label: Yes, pay for the cake
right.reaction: He ate it. Then the bin. The bin was load-bearing. The bakery's gone a bit wonky.

left.label: No. Return the cake.
left.reaction: The bakery won't take it back. It's been 'opened'. By a raccoon. From the inside.

cards.text: Boss. One more thing. For my present, could I have... the town? Just for the day. I'd give it back. Mostly. Can I?

right.label: Yes. Mayor for a day.
right.reaction: First act: all bins are now 'homes'. Second act: everything is a bin.

left.label: No. Here's a card instead.
left.reaction: He's read it nine times. He's laminated it. He's wearing it on a string.

cards.text: Boss. Best birthday ever. The cousins want to know if they can have birthdays too. There are four hundred cousins. Can they?

right.label: Yes. Everyone gets one.
right.reaction: It's somebody's birthday every day for a year. The bakery's hired more bakers. One is a raccoon.

left.label: No. One birthday. Yours.
left.reaction: They've all decided it's their birthday on the same day as Randy's. Next year will be a lot.

cards.text: Boss. I've written you a thank-you letter. It's forty pages. It's mostly drawings of bins. Read it out at the council?

right.label: Yes, read it out
right.reaction: Page 31 had a drawing of you. In a bin. Smiling. Half the council wept. The other half hissed.

left.label: No, I'll read it later
left.reaction: He's very understanding. He's left it on your chair. Forty pages. Slightly sticky. Lovingly.

cards.text: (Reginald the tortoise has been crossing Main Street since 1987. Today he is two feet from the other side.) Close the road for him?

right.label: Yes, close the road
right.reaction: Main Street is closed. A crowd has gathered. Bev's taking bets. Barb's confiscating the bets.

left.label: No. Traffic must flow.
left.reaction: The traffic flowed. Very carefully. Around a tortoise. At no miles an hour.

cards.text: Reginald is one foot from the kerb. The town has stopped work. Children were born, in the crowd, waiting. Hold a ceremony?

right.label: Yes, a ceremony
right.reaction: There's a ribbon. A brass band. Randy's selling commemorative bin lids. He's sold forty.

left.label: No fuss
left.reaction: No fuss. Just four thousand people silently staring at a tortoise. It's very tense.

cards.text: A lorry has stopped for Reginald. Behind the lorry, a bus. Behind the bus, the entire next county. They're all waiting. Divert them?

right.label: Yes, divert the traffic
right.reaction: Diverted. Through the park. Gerald directed it. Gerald's taken a toll. In bread.

left.label: No. They can wait.
left.reaction: They waited. They got out. They brought deckchairs. It's a festival now.

cards.text: (Reginald reaches the kerb. He stops. He looks back across Main Street. He turns round.) Let him go back?

right.label: Yes. It's his journey.
right.reaction: He's crossing back. It'll take another thirty-nine years. The crowd has settled in.

left.label: No. Carry him over.
left.reaction: You carried him. He did not enjoy it. He has looked at you once since. Once was enough.

cards.text: My client, Reginald, has been on Main Street longer than the road. He claims ownership. Of the road. Under squatters' rights. Settle?

right.label: Yes. Give him the road.
right.reaction: Reginald owns Main Street. Speed limit: tortoise. Bev has been banned from his road.

left.label: No. See you in court.
left.reaction: The hearing's set. Reginald set off for court this morning. It's in 2031.

cards.text: Boss. Reginald and I go way back. He was here before me. He's the only one who remembers when I was a baby. Make him an elder?

right.label: Yes. Town Elder.
right.reaction: He accepted. With a slow blink. It took eleven minutes. Best speech anyone's ever given.

left.label: No. He's a tortoise.
left.reaction: Reginald has started slowly turning to face you, wherever you are. It may take a week.

cards.text: The 1987 time capsule is due to be opened. It's buried under your office. Under the pond. Under the geese. Dig it up?

right.label: Yes, dig it up
right.reaction: The geese moved, for a fee. In bread. They've watched every shovel. Judging.

left.label: No. Leave it buried.
left.reaction: It's started knocking. From under the pond. In a pattern. Linda says it's Morse. It says 'OI'.

cards.text: Inside the capsule: a cassette, a slice of cheese, and a letter from the mayor of 1987. The mayor of 1987 was Randy. Read the letter?

right.label: Yes, read it
right.reaction: 'Dear future. I'm still here. I'm in a bin. Hello.' Randy has confirmed: he is, and he was.

left.label: No. Seal it again.
left.reaction: Randy is upset. 'I wrote that for you,' he says. 'Thirty-nine years ago. With a crayon.'

cards.text: The cheese from the capsule is the same cheese. Our cheese. It's been in two places at once since 1987. It hums at me. Investigate?

right.label: Yes, investigate
right.reaction: Dr Nora says the cheese is 'a bit quantum'. It's in the vault and on your desk. Both are humming.

left.label: No. Some things you leave.
left.reaction: Wise. The cheese seems relieved. Both of it.

cards.text: The cassette is a song. From 1987. It's called 'Bad Town Forever'. It's terrible. People are humming it anyway. Play it on the radio?

right.label: Yes, play it
right.reaction: It's number one. Of the one chart. The singer's been found. It's Reginald. Slowly, he's touring.

left.label: No. Bury it again.
left.reaction: Bev's got it on a loop on the scooter. At top volume. At top speed. You hear it everywhere, briefly.

cards.text: It's tradition to bury a new capsule for the year 2065. What goes in? We have room for one thing. Randy has volunteered.

right.label: Bury Randy (briefly)
right.reaction: Randy was buried for ninety seconds. He's posted a letter from inside. It says 'Dear future, hello.'

left.label: Bury a photo of the town
left.reaction: Gerald photobombed it. Every one. A goose in every frame. 2065 will think we were all geese.

cards.text: Your opponent this week is Gary, a vending machine. He's out of order. His slogan is 'OUT OF ORDER'. Voters find it honest. Debate him?

right.label: Yes, debate Gary
right.reaction: You spoke for ten minutes. Gary hummed. Then dropped a Twix. The crowd roared.

left.label: No. He's a machine.
left.reaction: 'MAYOR AFRAID OF SNACKS.' Gary's up four points. He's still out of order.

cards.text: Boss. I've had a look inside Gary. There's a raccoon in there. It's my cousin Terry. Terry is Gary. Expose him?

right.label: Yes. Expose Terry.
right.reaction: 'GARY IS TERRY.' Huge scandal. Terry has resigned. Gary is still standing. Gary has a new raccoon.

left.label: No. Leave Terry be.
left.reaction: Terry's grateful. Terry has dispensed you a free crisp. It's been in Terry's mouth.

cards.text: Mayor. Gary's polling well. I'd like to buy Gary. And put him in every building. All forty of him. Will you allow it?

right.label: Yes. Forty Garys.
right.reaction: Every building has a Gary. Every Gary is out of order. Every Gary is winning.

left.label: No. One Gary is enough.
left.reaction: Chad's bought a jukebox instead. It's running too. Its slogan is a song.

cards.text: (Gary has dispensed a small note. It says: 'I WILL GIVE YOU A FREE DRINK IF YOU DROP OUT.') Take the drink?

right.label: Yes, take the drink
right.reaction: It was a can of soup. Hot soup. You took the bribe. Marge has the photo.

left.label: No. I'm staying in.
left.reaction: Gary took it badly. He has dispensed every crisp he had. Onto you. In public.

cards.text: Someone has pushed Gary over. He's fine. He's on his back. Snacks everywhere. A crowd is eating his manifesto. Help him up?

right.label: Yes, help Gary up
right.reaction: You lifted him. Your back went. He dispensed you a plaster. Respect, between rivals.

left.label: No. Not my opponent.
left.reaction: 'MAYOR WALKS PAST FALLEN SNACK MACHINE.' The town is divided. Mostly against you.

cards.text: (Gary is back up. His display flickers. It says 'THANK U' or 'HANK U'. Hard to tell.) Shake hands?

right.label: Yes, shake hands
right.reaction: You shook his button. He dispensed a Twix. You split it. The town has never been so moved.

left.label: No. It's a vending machine.
left.reaction: His display now just says 'HMPH'. He's selling your face on a sticker. Out of order.

cards.text: Mayor! Bad Town's Got Talent! Tonight! You're the judge! Forty acts! Nine of them are Bev. Will you judge?

right.label: Yes, I'll judge
right.reaction: Wonderful! You're on the panel with Gerald and a chair. The chair is Chad's. Chad's late.

left.label: No. Get Randy to judge.
left.reaction: Randy's judging. He's given everything a ten. He's eaten the scorecards. All of them tens.

cards.text: (Act one: Marcel. He mimes being trapped in a box. For forty minutes. Nobody can tell if he's stuck.) Put him through?

right.label: Yes. Through!
right.reaction: He's through. He hasn't left the box. It's part of the act. It may not be part of the act.

left.label: No. Next!
left.reaction: He mimed walking off in tears. He has not walked off. He's still in the box. Weeping silently.

cards.text: Act two: the cousins. Forty raccoons. Their act is 'eating a bin, but as a dance'. It's beautiful, boss. Put them through?

right.label: Yes. Through!
right.reaction: Standing ovation. The bin is gone. So is the stage. So is Chad's chair. Chad's here now.

left.label: No. That's just eating.
left.reaction: Randy's crying. 'It was eating as a DANCE, boss.' Gerald honks in agreement.

cards.text: Act nine: me, dear. I'll be juggling chainsaws. On the scooter. Through a ring of fire. At forty miles an hour. Can I?

right.label: Yes. Go on, Bev.
right.reaction: She did it. Blindfolded. Backwards. The fire brigade asked for her autograph.

left.label: No. Health and safety.
left.reaction: I'll juggle normal saws, then. (She juggled normal saws. It was somehow worse.)

cards.text: (Final act: Clive the traffic cone. He stands there. For six minutes. The crowd is silent. Then they rise.) Crown Clive the winner?

right.label: Yes. Clive wins.
right.reaction: The cone has won Bad Town's Got Talent. Nobody can explain why. Everyone cried.

left.label: No. Bev wins.
left.reaction: Bev won. She did a lap of honour. Then nine more. She's still going. Nobody stops Bev.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has fallen in love. With the swan pedalo on the park pond. He would like your blessing.) Give it?

right.label: Yes. Blessing given.
right.reaction: HONK. (Gerald has proposed. With a breadstick. The pedalo didn't say no.)

left.label: No. It's a pedalo.
left.reaction: Gerald has written a letter to the pedalo explaining you're the problem. It's 'honk' 400 times.

cards.text: Gerald and the pedalo are getting married. Saturday. In your office pond. Four hundred geese are coming. Pay for the reception?

right.label: Yes, pay for it
right.reaction: Four hundred geese. One cake. No cake left. Some tables left. Some.

left.label: No. Bread only.
left.reaction: The geese have accepted. Grimly. They've brought their own bread. It's your bread.

cards.text: HONK. (The pedalo has been stolen from the pond. Gerald is in mourning. He suspects you. And Randy.) Find the pedalo?

right.label: Yes, find it
right.reaction: Found. It was in Randy's coat. He says 'it followed him home'. Gerald has bitten Randy.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: Gerald waited in the empty pond. By dawn the pedalo was back. Nobody knows how. Wedding's on.

cards.text: Boss. I've been asked to be Gerald's best man. I've written a speech. It's mostly about the time he bit me. Can I give it?

right.label: Yes. Give the speech.
right.reaction: Gerald wept. The pedalo said nothing. Randy got a standing honk.

left.label: No. Keep it short.
left.reaction: He said 'Gerald bit me once' and sat down. It was perfect. Gerald nodded. Approvingly.

cards.text: Gerald is asking you to officiate. You'd have to say 'you may now honk the bride'. On camera. Will you do it?

right.label: Yes. I'll officiate.
right.reaction: 'You may now honk the bride.' Four hundred geese honked at once. Three windows broke. Beautiful.

left.label: No. Get Randy to.
left.reaction: Randy officiated. He said 'you may now eat the cake'. Everyone did. Including the cake stand.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. The whole town has the hiccups. All of it. At the same time. In rhythm. It's started a beat. Declare an emergency?

right.label: Yes. Emergency.
right.reaction: Barb's announcement on the tannoy was mostly hiccups. People think it's a song.

left.label: No. Hold your breath.
left.reaction: Everyone held their breath. For a minute. Then hiccupped together. The bank's windows fell out.

cards.text: I can cure it, Mayor. One big shock. I need permission to make the whole town jump. At once. With a goose. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Do the goose.
right.reaction: Gerald honked through every loudspeaker. The town jumped. The hiccups stopped. Doug fainted.

left.label: No. Too risky.
left.reaction: The hiccups are in their third day. A choir has formed. It's very good. It's very tired.

cards.text: The town's hiccups have made it into the charts. 'Hic (Bad Town Remix)'. It's number one. Release it officially?

right.label: Yes, release it
right.reaction: We're rich. And still hiccupping. Our royalties are going on gripe water.

left.label: No. It's a medical issue.
left.reaction: Bootlegs everywhere. Randy's selling them from the coat. Every copy hiccups.

cards.text: The town's hiccups have finally stopped. Except mine. Mine never stopped. They started in 1994. Can I have the afternoon off?

right.label: Yes. Go home, Doug.
right.reaction: He went home. He hiccupped all the way. Rhythmically. A small crowd followed. They danced.

left.label: No. Hiccup at your desk.
left.reaction: He did the budget hiccupping. Every figure's doubled. We're accidentally rich.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. The giant inflatable duck from the carnival has broken loose. It's drifting over town. Blocking the sun. Shoot it down?

right.label: Yes. Bring it down.
right.reaction: Barb aimed. Then didn't. 'I can't,' she said. 'Look at its face.'

left.label: No. Let it drift.
left.reaction: The duck has eclipsed the bakery. The bread's gone dark. Nobody will eat it. Gerald will.

cards.text: Boss. I've climbed onto the duck. I'm on the duck. I can see my bin from here. I'm going to steer it. Shall I?

right.label: Yes. Steer the duck.
right.reaction: He landed it in the park pond. Gently. Then waved. Then the duck sat on him. He's fine.

left.label: No. Get off the duck.
left.reaction: He let go. He floated down on a bin lid. He's fine. The duck is not. The duck is in the next town.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has seen the giant duck. He is in love. Again. He's left the pedalo a note.) Allow Gerald to court the duck?

right.label: Yes. Follow your heart.
right.reaction: Gerald flew up to the duck. They've been circling all day. The duck is losing air. Gerald isn't.

left.label: No. You're married.
left.reaction: Gerald has stopped speaking to you. He was already only honking. Now he's honking less.

cards.text: A letter from the carnival. They want their duck back. Or forty thousand pounds. It's the only duck they have. Pay them?

right.label: Yes. Pay for the duck.
right.reaction: The duck is ours now. It's in the park. People picnic under it. It's a very good roof.

left.label: No. Return the duck.
left.reaction: You returned the duck. It drifted back the next day. It likes it here. So does Gerald.

cards.text: Boss. Bad news. Every sock in Bad Town has gone. Overnight. Every one. It wasn't me. I need you to know that before you search the coat.

right.label: Search the coat
right.reaction: Barb searched it. Four thousand socks. Also Doug. Doug says it was 'warm'.

left.label: No. I believe you.
left.reaction: Randy wept. 'Nobody's ever believed me.' He's wearing nine socks. On one foot.

cards.text: The socks have been returned. None of them match. Not one pair. Every single person in town is mismatched. Order a sock swap?

right.label: Yes. Town sock swap.
right.reaction: The swap took nine hours. In the gym. It was emotional. Some socks found their way home.

left.label: No. Mismatched is fine.
left.reaction: Mismatched socks are fashion now. Chad's bought a sock factory. It makes odd socks.

cards.text: With no socks, the town's feet are cold. The school's in slippers. The bank's in slippers. Barb's in slippers. Fund emergency socks?

right.label: Yes. Emergency socks.
right.reaction: Four thousand socks arrived. All the same. Randy has nine already. He's eaten two.

left.label: No. Toughen up.
left.reaction: Morale has hit the floor. Specifically, a very cold floor.

cards.text: Boss. Since we're being honest. The cousins have been using the socks as sleeping bags. Could they keep a few? For the babies?

right.label: Yes. For the babies.
right.reaction: Forty tiny raccoons in forty tiny socks. It's on the front page. Nobody has been angry since.

left.label: No. Socks are for feet.
left.reaction: They gave them back. Warm. Every sock smells of bin now. Every foot in town smells of bin.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. It's Tuesday. Again. It was Tuesday yesterday. Everybody remembers yesterday. Except the calendar. Declare it Wednesday?

right.label: Yes. It's Wednesday.
right.reaction: Declared. The calendar disagrees. Mr Whiskers is representing the calendar.

left.label: No. Enjoy Tuesday.
left.reaction: Tuesday again. Barb's arrested the same burglar three times. He's asked for a different Tuesday.

cards.text: My client, the calendar, objects. It insists it is Tuesday. It is very firm. It has a page for this. Settle out of court?

right.label: Yes. Settle.
right.reaction: Settled. It's 'Tuesday, Part Two'. Everyone's agreed to pretend. It's working. Mostly.

left.label: No. To court.
left.reaction: The trial is set for Wednesday. Which never comes. Mr Whiskers has billed us for every Tuesday.

cards.text: Mayor, it's been Tuesday for six days. I've done the same budget six times. It's the same budget. I'm losing my mind. Can I skip a day?

right.label: Yes. Skip Tuesday.
right.reaction: You skipped it. It's Thursday. Wednesday is missing. Randy says he 'doesn't have it'.

left.label: No. Do it again.
left.reaction: Seventh time. Doug made one change. He drew a smiley face. It's the best budget he's ever done.

cards.text: Boss. I found Wednesday. It was in the coat. It's a bit crumpled. Do you want it back?

right.label: Yes. Give me Wednesday.
right.reaction: Wednesday is back. Everyone wept. Even Tuesday. It's been a long week.

left.label: No. Keep it.
left.reaction: Randy now has his own Wednesday. He spends it alone. In a bin. Happily.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. The ice cream van is stuck playing its tune. At full volume. It's driving in circles. Round the town. It won't stop. Stop it?

right.label: Yes. Stop the van.
right.reaction: Barb chased it. On foot. For an hour. It's ice cream. It's always one street ahead.

left.label: No. Let it play.
left.reaction: The tune is in everyone's head. Babies hum it. Dogs hum it. Gerald honks it. Badly.

cards.text: I can catch that van, dear. Scooter's tuned. I've had a scone. Just say the word. Shall I?

right.label: Yes. Go, Bev.
right.reaction: Bev caught it in nine seconds. She's driving it now. Faster. The tune's sped up. It's techno.

left.label: No. Let Barb handle it.
left.reaction: Barb's still running. She's in the next county. The van's behind her now. She hasn't noticed.

cards.text: Boss. Inside the van there's four tons of ice cream. Melting. It's very hot. The cousins have formed a queue. Can we have it?

right.label: Yes. Free ice cream.
right.reaction: The whole town ate ice cream. The tune stopped. Nobody noticed. They were too happy.

left.label: No. It's evidence.
left.reaction: The evidence melted. It's in the drains. The drains are very happy. The cousins are in the drains.

cards.text: The ice cream van ran out of petrol. Beautiful silence. The ice cream man has written in. He wants compensation for 'emotional strain'. Pay him?

right.label: Yes. Pay him.
right.reaction: He's bought a quieter van. It plays a single, sad note. People still queue.

left.label: No. He started it.
left.reaction: He's taken up the trumpet in protest. He only knows the tune.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. Heatwave. The cheese in the vault is melting. It's coming out under the door. It's heading for the river. Stop it?

right.label: Yes. Stop the cheese.
right.reaction: Barb built a dam. Of crackers. It's holding. Mostly. It smells amazing.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: The river is fondue now. It's on the brochure. Gerald has been dipping bread since dawn.

cards.text: The cheese has stopped. At the cracker dam. It's... reforming. It's humming. It's taller than me. Shall I evacuate?

right.label: Yes. Evacuate Doug.
right.reaction: Doug's safe. The cheese has taken his desk. It's doing his job. It's doing it better.

left.label: No. Stand firm.
left.reaction: Doug stood firm. The cheese stood firmer. They've come to an arrangement. Doug won't say what.

cards.text: Mayor. A river of fondue. Outside my restaurant. This is the greatest day of my life. Can I put tables on it?

right.label: Yes. Tables on the river.
right.reaction: Sal's River Fondue is booked out for a year. The tyre is head chef. It floats.

left.label: No. It's a river.
left.reaction: Sal is serving it anyway. From a rowing boat. With a ladle. Nobody can stop him.

cards.text: hmmmmmmm. (The cheese has cooled. It's reshaped itself. It's shaped like you. It seems pleased.) Put it on display?

right.label: Yes. Display it.
right.reaction: Four thousand came to see a cheese of you. Randy ate the nose. You've never been more popular.

left.label: No. Back in the vault.
left.reaction: It went quietly. It's still shaped like you. It's waiting in the dark. Humming your name.

cards.text: Draft law on your desk: everyone must nap from two to three. Randy wrote it. He's asleep on it. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Two o'clock. The whole town lay down. Crime stopped. Barb was asleep at the scene.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Randy woke up. He read the 'no'. He went back to sleep. On your hand.

cards.text: Draft law: all cats must wear little hats. Coach Dunk wrote it. Mr Whiskers has already filed an objection. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Every cat in a little hat. Mr Whiskers' is a wig. He's suing himself. He's winning.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Mr Whiskers has sent a thank-you note. It's a dead mouse. In a little hat.

cards.text: Draft law: beige is now the town's official colour. Doug wrote it. He's wearing beige. He is beige. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Everything's beige. Gerald is fine with it. Randy is not. He's grey on principle.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Doug's sad. He'd painted the treasury. In anticipation. It was already beige.

cards.text: Draft law: geese must give way to cars. Gerald has read it. Gerald is standing on your desk. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Gerald has not given way. Not once. Gerald has been ticketed. Gerald ate the ticket.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Gerald nodded. Once. Then he gave way to a car. Just to show it was his idea.

cards.text: Draft law: Tuesdays are renamed 'Kevins'. In honour of the pothole. Randy is crying already. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Next Kevin, the town met at Kevin. Kevin did nothing. It was the best Kevin ever.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Randy is calling it Kevin anyway. 'See you Kevin, boss.' Everyone's started saying it.

cards.text: Draft law: vending machines may not run for office. Gary would be disqualified. Randy says 'it's dirty, boss. I love it.' Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Disqualify Gary.
right.reaction: Gary's off the ballot. He's running as a write-in. Every vote for him is a crisp packet.

left.label: No. Beat him fairly.
left.reaction: Gary has dispensed you a small biscuit. Respect. It's slightly stale. So is respect.

cards.text: Randy is sneaking slices of his own birthday cake into his coat. Grab the cake back when he's not looking.

right.label: Got it!
right.reaction: Boss! I was just keeping it warm. In my coat. With my cousins.

left.label: He saw you
left.reaction: Randy saw you coming. The whole cake is in the coat now. The coat burped.

cards.text: Reginald is about to bite the mayoral ribbon. Very slowly. Move it before he looks round. He will look round slowly.

right.label: Moved it
right.reaction: He looked round. Slowly. The ribbon was gone. He looked at you. Slowly. You'll never forget it.

left.label: Bitten
left.reaction: Ribbon gone. Reginald is chewing it. He'll be chewing it until Thursday.

cards.text: Linda's about to read the time capsule letter aloud. It mentions your school nickname. Pocket it while she looks for her glasses.

right.label: Pocketed
right.reaction: Nobody heard 'Captain Crumbs'. Except you. In your head. Forever.

left.label: She read it
left.reaction: 'Captain Crumbs.' The Bugle has it. So does the town. So does Gerald. He honks it.

cards.text: Gary's front panel is ajar. Your opponent's manifesto is inside. Grab it while his display is off.

right.label: Got the manifesto
right.reaction: It's a list of snacks. That's the whole manifesto. It's strangely moving.

left.label: His light came on
left.reaction: Gary has dispensed a receipt. It says 'THIEF'. It's on the front page. In capitals.

cards.text: Marcel has mimed a velvet rope in front of the talent show trophy. Steal it for Bev before he turns round.

right.label: Got it!
right.reaction: Bev has the trophy. Marcel has mimed a different trophy. He's polishing it. Proudly.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: Marcel mimed handcuffs on you. They felt very real. You were stuck there an hour.

cards.text: Gerald is guarding the wedding cake. One slice for the Mayor. Grab it while he's honking at a pedalo.

right.label: Got a slice!
right.reaction: Delicious. Bread cake. With bread icing. Gerald never knew.

left.label: He turned round
left.reaction: HONK. (He took the slice, and your shoe, and your dignity.)

cards.text: The lost property office has started returning things to people who never lost them. Barb got a horse. Ask it to stop?

right.label: Yes, make it stop
right.reaction: It stopped. It has kept the horse. Barb is heartbroken. She'd named it.

left.label: No. Let it give.
left.reaction: Doug got a trumpet. Pam got a canoe. You got a raccoon. It's Randy. He says he was 'lost'.

cards.text: I'd like the horse back, Mayor. I've visited it every day. It knows my voice. It's in the lost property office. Can I have it?

right.label: Yes. Have the horse.
right.reaction: Barb rides to work now. Arrests are down. Hugs are up. The horse is called Sergeant Hay.

left.label: No. Rules are rules.
left.reaction: Barb has filed the horse as 'lost'. Then found it. It's hers now, legally. She checked.

cards.text: Boss. The lost property office gave me to you. So I'm yours. Legally. Like a hat. Can I have a little shelf?

right.label: Yes. A little shelf.
right.reaction: He sits on the shelf. All day. Very proud. He's labelled himself. 'BOSS'S RACCOON. DO NOT LOSE.'

left.label: No shelves for raccoons
left.reaction: He's hidden himself in the lost property office again. He's waiting to be found. By you.

cards.text: I've printed Bad Town Bucks. Our own currency. One Buck equals one Buck. The notes have my face on. Make them legal?

right.label: Yes, legal tender
right.reaction: Bad Town Bucks are live. Sal's charging nine of them for soup. Nobody knows if that's a lot.

left.label: No. Pounds only.
left.reaction: Chad's using them as napkins. In public. He wants you to see.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. I'll swap your Bad Town Bucks for acorns. One Buck, one acorn. Chad calls it 'an insult'. Accept my rate?

right.label: Yes. Acorns it is.
right.reaction: The squirrels are rich. Chad's broke. In acorns. He's started burying things.

left.label: No. Hold out for two.
left.reaction: Two acorns a Buck. Chad's thrilled. Nutkins has sent a note. It's an acorn. An angry one.

cards.text: The fountain has started granting wishes. Actual wishes. Someone wished for a pony. Now there's a pony. Shut it off?

right.label: Yes, shut it off
right.reaction: Off. Silence. A man was halfway through a wish. He's now half a millionaire.

left.label: No. Wish away.
left.reaction: Forty ponies. A rollercoaster. Bev wished for 'more speed'. Bev is now faster. Somehow.

cards.text: Boss. Before you turned it off, I made one wish. I wished you'd be happy. Are you? Be honest.

right.label: Yes. I am.
right.reaction: He's wept into the fountain. It turned back on. Then off. A small rainbow came out.

left.label: No. Not really.
left.reaction: 'Me neither, boss.' You sat together by the fountain. You both feel better.

cards.text: Mayor. Someone wished the budget would balance. It has. It's balanced. On a pony. The pony is very nervous. Can we keep the pony?

right.label: Yes, keep the pony
right.reaction: The pony is Deputy Treasurer. It's very good. Doug has stopped crying. He's learning to ride.

left.label: No. Return the pony.
left.reaction: The pony wished itself back. With friends. The treasury is a stable now.

cards.text: Stormy Steve has quit. He's been replaced by a weathervane. A rooster. It's 100% accurate. It's also a rooster. Keep it?

right.label: Yes. Keep the rooster.
right.reaction: 'Cock-a-doodle-sun.' Ratings are up. Steve has been seen outside the studio. Watching.

left.label: No. Bring back Steve.
left.reaction: Steve is back. He's furious. He's forecasting 'betrayal'. With a light breeze.

cards.text: Mayor. I'd like a rematch. Me against the rooster. A forecast-off. Winner takes the weather. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Forecast-off.
right.reaction: Steve predicted rain. The rooster predicted sun. It hailed. They've agreed to share. Nobody's happy.

left.label: No. No rematches.
left.reaction: Steve's predicting doom. It's only the second time he's been right. It rained. On him.

cards.text: Marcel the mime wants to open a restaurant. Invisible food. Invisible prices. Real bills. Grant the licence?

right.label: Yes, grant it
right.reaction: It's full every night. Nobody can tell if they've eaten. Everyone leaves starving and delighted.

left.label: No. Food must exist.
left.reaction: He's appealing. Silently. Outside your window. With a mimed placard. It's a good placard.

cards.text: Mayor! The invisible restaurant got three stars! THREE! I serve REAL TYRES and I have TWO. Ban invisible food?

right.label: Yes. Ban invisible food.
right.reaction: Banned. Marcel served one final invisible meal. Everyone wept. Silently. Sal ate it. Twice.

left.label: No. Let him cook.
left.reaction: Sal has gone invisible too. In protest. His tyres are now 'imagined'. Business is booming.

cards.text: An owl has moved into the library. It just stares. It's very wise-looking. Borrowing is down. Evict the owl?

right.label: Yes. Evict it.
right.reaction: It left. It looked back once. It knew. You'll never know what it knew.

left.label: No. It's wise.
left.reaction: Students ask it questions. It says 'hoo'. They say they've learned something. They have.

cards.text: The owl has been seen in your office. Staring at you. All day. Readers want to know if you've done something. Have you?

right.label: Yes. I'll confess.
right.reaction: You confessed to taking an extra biscuit in 2019. The owl blinked. It forgave you. Marge printed it.

left.label: No. Nothing.
left.reaction: The owl kept staring. You cracked by noon. You confessed to everything. Even things you didn't do.

cards.text: Big idea. Bad Town Bike Share. Forty bikes. App-controlled. Randy has volunteered to 'look after' them. Launch it?

right.label: Yes, launch it
right.reaction: All forty bikes are in Randy's coat. He says they're 'docked'. Technically.

left.label: No. Walk.
left.reaction: Brayden's launched it anyway. One bike. It's his. You have to ask him. He says no.

cards.text: Boss. The bikes are safe. In the coat. But the cousins have learned to ride them. Can they keep them?

right.label: Yes. Raccoon bikes.
right.reaction: Forty raccoons on forty bikes. They do laps of Main Street. Reginald finds it very stressful.

left.label: No. Give them back.
left.reaction: They gave them back. Every bike has a bell now. Every bell is a raccoon. You'll see.

cards.text: The new road signs have arrived. They're all spelled wrong. 'BAD TONW.' 'SKOOL.' 'MANE STREET.' Reprint them?

right.label: Yes, reprint
right.reaction: Reprinted. They say 'BAD TOWN'. So does the school. And the bank. The printer's stuck.

left.label: No. Keep them.
left.reaction: Tourists love them. 'Wellcome to Bad Tonw.' Randy put the spare letters in the coat.

cards.text: The printer only prints 'BAD TOWN' now. On everything. Our budget says 'BAD TOWN BAD TOWN BAD TOWN'. It's... accurate. Replace it?

right.label: Yes, new printer
right.reaction: The new printer only prints 'SORRY'. On everything. It's very polite. It's very unhelpful.

left.label: No. It's honest.
left.reaction: The council minutes are just 'BAD TOWN' four hundred times. Everyone agreed with all of it.

cards.text: (Clive the traffic cone has turned up at your office. He has not said why. He just stands there. Orange. Patient.) Let him in?

right.label: Yes. Come in, Clive.
right.reaction: He's been in your office all week. Standing. It's actually quite calming. Like a lamp.

left.label: No. Shut the door.
left.reaction: He's standing outside the door. You can see his tip through the glass. He's very patient.

cards.text: Boss. Clive and I have been talking. Well, I talked. Clive listened. He'd like a job. He's very good at standing. Hire him?

right.label: Yes. Hire Clive.
right.reaction: Clive is now Head of Roadworks. Crime is down. Roadworks are up. He stands at all of them.

left.label: No. He's a cone.
left.reaction: Randy's given Clive a hat. It's a smaller cone. Clive seems moved. Hard to tell.

cards.text: I found a dinosaur bone in the park! It's very big. It's very old. Dr Nora says it's 'a bit chicken'. Can we dig for more?

right.label: Yes, dig!
right.reaction: The whole town's digging. They've found forty bones. All chicken. Sal is very quiet.

left.label: No. It's a chicken.
left.reaction: Timmy has declared you 'an enemy of science'. On a poster. With crayon. It's everywhere.

cards.text: Good news: I've built a dinosaur out of the bones. Bad news: it's alive. It's a giant chicken. It's in the gym. Keep it?

right.label: Yes. Keep the chicken.
right.reaction: Its name is Doris. She lays eggs the size of Doug. Breakfast is sorted for a year.

left.label: No. Return it to the past.
left.reaction: We couldn't. She's a chicken. She's now in the park. Gerald has declared war. It's even.

cards.text: Boss. I'd like to pay tax. I've never paid tax. I've saved up. It's in the coat. It's mostly buttons. Will you accept it?

right.label: Yes. Thank you, Randy.
right.reaction: 4,000 buttons. Doug has counted them. Twice. Doug says it's 'the most honest money we've ever had'.

left.label: No. Keep your buttons.
left.reaction: He looked so sad. He's put the buttons back in the coat. One button rolled out. It's still rolling.

cards.text: Boss. Now I'm a taxpayer, I'd like a say. My say is: more bins. That's all. That's my whole say. Approve?

right.label: Yes. More bins.
right.reaction: Four hundred new bins. Randy has visited every one. He's very fulfilled. So are the bins.

left.label: No. Enough bins.
left.reaction: He's written to his MP. His MP is Gerald. Gerald honked. Randy feels heard.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has opened a bakery. It sells bread. It's all your bread. He stole it. He's selling it back to you.) Buy some?

right.label: Yes, buy some
right.reaction: It's very good bread. It should be. It's your bread. You'd like the recipe. It's yours.

left.label: No. That's my bread.
left.reaction: Barb has arrested Gerald. He's honked his one phone call. Mr Whiskers is on his way.

cards.text: My client, Mr Whiskers, is suing the moon. It keeps him awake at night. It's very bright. Will the town join the case?

right.label: Yes. Join the case.
right.reaction: The moon has not responded. My client considers that an admission. Damages: a nap.

left.label: No. Leave the moon.
left.reaction: My client has decided to sue you instead. For not suing the moon. It's the same case, really.

cards.text: I'm going skydiving on Thursday, dear. For my ninety-eighth. Out of a helicopter. Into the pond. Can I borrow the helicopter?

right.label: Yes. Borrow it.
right.reaction: She jumped. She landed in the pond. On Gerald. Gerald is honoured. Gerald is also flat.

left.label: No. Too dangerous.
left.reaction: She jumped off the church roof instead. With an umbrella. She's fine. The umbrella isn't.

cards.text: (A note slides under Doug's door. It says PROMOTION. YOUR OFFICE. PLEASE. It's from the cheese.) Give it Doug's office?

right.label: Yes, give it Doug's office
right.reaction: Doug's in the cupboard now. The cheese is in charge. The budget smells. It balances.

left.label: No. Doug stays.
left.reaction: The cheese has taken it well. It has started a petition. It has four thousand signatures. All 'hmm'.

cards.text: Mayor! Bad Town needs a sports team! I'm thinking... the Bad Town Geese! Gerald's agreed to be the mascot! Fund it?

right.label: Yes. Go Geese!
right.reaction: First match: lost 40–0. Gerald bit the referee. The crowd went wild. Best day of their lives.

left.label: No. No sport.
left.reaction: Coach has started training anyway. Alone. In the park. Shouting at trees.

cards.text: The Geese have lost nine games! The fans love it! They want an away kit! It's a bin bag! Randy designed it! Approve?

right.label: Yes. Bin bag kit.
right.reaction: The kit sold out. Everyone in town wears one. You can't tell fans from rubbish. Randy's thrilled.

left.label: No. Proper kit.
left.reaction: The proper kit arrived. Everyone wore bin bags over it anyway. Tradition.

cards.text: Crime is up. Someone's stolen the police station's doors. Just the doors. I'm working in a draught. Pay for new doors?

right.label: Yes. New doors.
right.reaction: New doors. Randy's offered to 'look after' the old doors. He's already wearing one.

left.label: No. Curtains.
left.reaction: Curtains. Nobody knows if we're open. We're not sure either.

cards.text: There's a protest outside City Hall. They've brought signs. And snacks. And chairs. They're settling in. Go and talk to them?

right.label: Yes. Talk to them.
right.reaction: You listened for an hour. They gave you a snack. Everyone feels slightly better.

left.label: No. Wait it out.
left.reaction: They've built a shed. It's got a kettle. They're never leaving.

cards.text: Mayor. We're nearly out of money. I've been selling my own sandwiches. I've made eleven pounds. Sell the town clock?

right.label: Yes. Sell the clock.
right.reaction: Sold. Nobody knows what time it is. Randy's started telling people. He's always wrong. Confidently.

left.label: No. Tax the geese.
left.reaction: The geese have paid. In bread. We're rich in bread. Doug's trying to bank it.

cards.text: Business is booming! I'd like to buy the town hall. I'll rent it back to you. Very reasonable. Per hour. Sell it?

right.label: Yes. Sell City Hall.
right.reaction: Chad Hall. The doors open with a credit card. Yours doesn't work.

left.label: No.
left.reaction: Fine. I'll buy the building next door. And look in.

cards.text: The pigeon from last week is back. It has a lawyer. The lawyer is a smaller pigeon. They want your stapler. Again. Hand it over?

right.label: Yes. Take it.
right.reaction: Coo. (It has stapled a thank-you note to your forehead. Gently. Professionally.)

left.label: No. Not again.
left.reaction: The small pigeon has served you papers. They're crumbs. Legally binding crumbs.

cards.text: The pigeons have opened a stationery shop. In the clock tower. They only sell your stapler. It's always in stock. Shut it down?

right.label: Yes, shut it
right.reaction: Shut. They've gone mobile. A pigeon with a stapler is following you. It's patient.

left.label: No. Buy it back.
left.reaction: £40. For your own stapler. It came with a loyalty card. Ten staples, one free.

cards.text: Boss. Winter's coming. The cousins want to hibernate. In City Hall. In the filing cabinets. It's very cosy. Can they?

right.label: Yes. Sleep tight.
right.reaction: Four hundred raccoons in the filing. The 'R' drawer snores. Nobody can find anything. Nobody minds.

left.label: No. Not the filing.
left.reaction: They're hibernating in the coat. All of them. Randy's very warm. He can't move. He's fine.

cards.text: Mayor. The tax records are in the filing cabinet. With a raccoon asleep on them. He growls if I touch them. Wake him?

right.label: Yes. Wake him.
right.reaction: You woke him. He did your taxes. Grumpily. Perfectly. He's gone back to sleep. On the receipt.

left.label: No. Let him sleep.
left.reaction: We're filing on time next year. Or spring. When he wakes. He's dreaming. About bins.

cards.text: (A second traffic cone has appeared next to Clive. Clive seems... happy? Marge is calling it 'a relationship'.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Love is love.
right.reaction: The cones stand together on Main Street. People leave flowers. Traffic goes round. Tenderly.

left.label: No. One cone per road.
left.reaction: You moved the second cone. Clive has turned slightly. Towards you. Nobody saw him move.

cards.text: Mayor. There are forty cones on Main Street now. Nobody put them there. They're in a circle. Around your car. Move them?

right.label: Yes, move them
right.reaction: Moved. They were back by morning. In a heart shape. Clive in the middle. It's a lot.

left.label: No. Walk to work.
left.reaction: You walked. It was nice, actually. Clive watched you leave. Proudly.

cards.text: The giant chicken has laid an egg. It's the size of a car. It's warm. It's in the car park. It's hatching. Evacuate?

right.label: Yes, evacuate
right.reaction: The car park's empty. The egg cracked. Out came... a normal chicken. Small. Very small. Embarrassed.

left.label: No. Watch it hatch.
left.reaction: Four thousand people watched. Out came a duck. Nobody can explain it. Gerald's furious.

cards.text: Boss. A man has come from the council of 1987. He says I owe a library book. From when I was mayor. Pay my fine?

right.label: Yes. Pay Randy's fine.
right.reaction: Paid. Randy's so grateful he's returned the book. It's a different book. It's 'Bins: A History'.

left.label: No. Pay your own fine.
left.reaction: He's paying it in instalments. One button a week. It'll take until 2140. He's very committed.

cards.text: The school lunch lady has gone on strike. She's been replaced by Gerald. He serves bread. Only bread. Mostly stolen. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Bread for all.
right.reaction: The children love it. Gerald's never been happier. The lunch lady wants her job back. Tough.

left.label: No. Get her back.
left.reaction: She's back. She's added bread to the menu. As a tribute. Gerald approves. Grudgingly.

cards.text: The ghost book club wants to meet in your office. At midnight. They're reading 'Leadership'. The cheese recommended it. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Midnight meetings.
right.reaction: Your office is cold in the mornings now. Someone's left notes in the margins. Very good notes.

left.label: No ghosts after hours
left.reaction: They've moved to your car. You can hear them on the drive home. They hated the ending.

cards.text: Bev has started a taxi service. She charges by the second. Her taxi is the scooter. Nobody's ever been late. Licence her?

right.label: Yes, licence her
right.reaction: 'Bev Cabs.' Two passengers at a time. One is screaming. One is Doug. He uses it daily.

left.label: No. Too fast.
left.reaction: She's running it anyway. Unlicensed. The meter is a stopwatch. It's always under ten seconds.

cards.text: Readers want a museum. 'The Museum of Bad Town.' Randy's offered his coat as the main exhibit. Open it?

right.label: Yes, open the museum
right.reaction: The coat is behind glass. Things move inside it. Visitors scream. Five stars.

left.label: No museum
left.reaction: Randy's opened it anyway. In the coat. Admission: one crisp. It's very small. It's very popular.

cards.text: (Councillor Pebbles has tabled a motion. It's a turnip. He's put it on the table. He's staring at you.) Second the turnip?

right.label: Yes. I second it.
right.reaction: The turnip passed. It went to committee. Pebbles ate the committee.

left.label: No. That's a turnip.
left.reaction: Pebbles is filibustering. Six hours of bleating. Nobody can leave. Bev's asleep.

cards.text: (Councillor Pebbles has gone viral. #GoatVotes is trending. A lawnmower company wants to sponsor him. He's eaten their letter.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Get that sponsor.
right.reaction: In the advert, he eats the lawnmower. Sales are up 400%. Nobody understands why.

left.label: No. He's a councillor.
left.reaction: He's furious. He ate the offer letter. And the envelope. And Mr Flaps's hat.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. It's Thank-You Card Day. I've swallowed every card in town. For safety. Shall I deliver them now?

right.label: Yes. Deliver them.
right.reaction: Delivered. By coughing. On doorsteps. Wetly. People were still very touched.

left.label: No. Keep them safe.
left.reaction: He's holding 9,000 cards. He's sitting on the post office roof like a large egg.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. My cousin's visiting. Mrs Flaps. Also a pelican. Twice the beak. She'd like a job. Hire her?

right.label: Yes. Two Flaps.
right.reaction: Twice as fast. Twice as damp. They argue over every parcel. It's always in both of them.

left.label: No. One Flaps only.
left.reaction: Mrs Flaps opened a rival post office. Faster. Wetter. Mr Flaps won't discuss it.

cards.text: Wooo. Wendy here. A new ghost moved in. Derek. He's not a real ghost. He's a man in a sheet. Evict him?

right.label: Yes. Evict Derek.
right.reaction: Derek's gone. He took his sheet. He just wanted friends.

left.label: No. Derek stays.
left.reaction: Derek's thrilled. He says 'boo', then apologises. Everyone loves Derek.

cards.text: Mayor. Wendy's started ghost tours. She charges double. Very spooky. Also completely untaxed. Tax the ghost?

right.label: Yes. Tax the ghost.
right.reaction: She paid in coins from 1890. Doug had them valued. They're worth a fortune. Doug screamed.

left.label: No. Let her earn.
left.reaction: Sold out every night. Tourists leave very scared and very full of cake.

cards.text: Big Carl. It's raining. Every puddle in town is a danger. I need twelve more lifeguards. With whistles. Okay?

right.label: Yes. Twelve more Carls.
right.reaction: Twelve lifeguards whistling at puddles. Nobody's drowned. Nobody can hear anything.

left.label: No. You're enough.
left.reaction: He's guarding every puddle himself. Running. In flippers. He's surprisingly fast.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. Big Carl wants me to forecast puddles. Nobody can do that. He's blowing his whistle at me. Make him stop?

right.label: Yes. Whistle down.
right.reaction: Whistle confiscated. Carl just points at puddles now. Meaningfully.

left.label: No. Forecast puddles.
left.reaction: Steve forecasts puddles. He's always wrong. Carl guards the wrong ones. Somehow it works.

cards.text: (Kevin the pothole is up for Landmark of the Year. Rival nominee: Reginald the tortoise, still crossing the road.) Back Kevin?

right.label: Yes. Kevin!
right.reaction: Kevin won. Reginald fell into him on the way to the ceremony. They're friends now. Sort of.

left.label: No. Back Reginald.
left.reaction: Reginald won. He's still crossing over to collect it. Kevin is sulking. Deeper.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull has opened a 'Lost Property Office'. Everything in it was stolen by Lorraine.) Shut it down?

right.label: Yes. Shut it.
right.reaction: Shut. She's moved it to your roof. Your car keys are up there. And your car, somehow.

left.label: No. Let her trade.
left.reaction: Business is booming. People pay to get their own sandwiches back. She does a loyalty card.

cards.text: (Lorraine has drawn up a peace treaty with the Goose Union. It's on a napkin. Gerald has already honked on it.) Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Sign the napkin.
right.reaction: Seagulls get the seafront. Geese get the pond. Pigeons get nothing. Pigeons are drafting a reply.

left.label: No. Not on a napkin.
left.reaction: Gerald and Lorraine have both declared war on you instead. They've never been closer.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot would like to replace school dinners with mice. 'High in protein. Very fresh.') Approve the menu?

right.label: Yes. Mice for all.
right.reaction: Nobody ate them. The mice were relieved. They've joined the school. They're doing well in maths.

left.label: No. Normal dinners.
left.reaction: Normal dinners served. Hoot ate the dinner lady's sandwich. He apologised in a long, sad hoot.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot has set the end-of-year exam. It's one question: 'Who?' Nobody has passed.) Change the exam?

right.label: Yes. Easier questions.
right.reaction: New question: 'Who? (multiple choice)'. Everybody passed. Hoot is disappointed in all of you.

left.label: No. Standards matter.
left.reaction: National news: 'BAD TOWN SCHOOL HARDEST IN THE COUNTRY'. Timmy got 'a hoot'. Hoot says that counts.

cards.text: (Trevor the moth has a new love. Your phone screen. He sits on it during calls. He's on it now.) Let him stay?

right.label: Yes. Love wins.
right.reaction: Every call has Trevor in it. He's on speaker. He says nothing. People find it calming.

left.label: No. Shoo him off.
left.reaction: Shoo'd. He's moved to the town hall telly. He's on the news now. Every night. Just sitting there.

cards.text: Mayor, Trevor the moth has a column in the Bugle. It's called 'Light'. Every week it just says 'light'. It's our best seller. Expand it?

right.label: Yes. Two pages.
right.reaction: Two pages of 'light'. Readers call it the only honest thing in the paper. Marge is furious and rich.

left.label: No. One word is plenty.
left.reaction: He's started a rival paper. One word. 'Lamp.' It's outselling the Bugle.

cards.text: (Toby the oak tree would like to run in the Bad Town Marathon. He's been practising. He has moved four inches.) Let him enter?

right.label: Yes. Run, Toby.
right.reaction: The race finished hours ago. Toby is still on the start line. The crowd stayed. They're chanting.

left.label: No. Trees can't run.
left.reaction: He's leaning towards the finish line. Very slowly. Very determined. Marge has a weekly update.

cards.text: (Toby has reached the finish line. It took six days. The marathon committee wants to give him a medal. Made of wood.) Approve the medal?

right.label: Yes. A wooden medal.
right.reaction: He's wearing it. Woodpeckers keep visiting it. Toby says it's the proudest day of his life.

left.label: No. It's in poor taste.
left.reaction: A metal one, then. It's very heavy. Toby has bent slightly to the left. It suits him.

cards.text: It's hot. I'm ninety-seven. I'm swimming the river. The whole length. In my good hat. Close the river for me?

right.label: Yes. Close the river.
right.reaction: River closed. Four hundred people on the banks. Bev's doing backstroke. In the hat.

left.label: No. Share with the ducks.
left.reaction: She's swimming anyway. Between two pedalos. She's overtaken one.

cards.text: Big Carl. Bev is in the river. I've trained twelve years for this. It's my moment. Permission to save Bev?

right.label: Yes. Go, Carl.
right.reaction: He dived in. She was fine. He wasn't. Bev towed him to the bank. Two heroes.

left.label: No. She's fine.
left.reaction: He's on the bank, whistle in mouth, trembling. She waved. He cried.

cards.text: Mayor, Bev's been swimming six hours. She's stopped mid-river for a sandwich. Someone has to deliver it. Send a boat?

right.label: Yes. Send a boat.
right.reaction: The boat brought the sandwich. Bev complained about the crusts. Kept swimming.

left.label: No. She'll manage.
left.reaction: Mr Flaps delivered it. By beak. Wetly. She ate it anyway.

cards.text: I've done it. The whole river. They want to name it after me. 'The Bev'. Is that allowed?

right.label: Yes. The River Bev.
right.reaction: The signs are up. The ducks have moved in. Bev has never been prouder.

left.label: No. It's the River Bad.
left.reaction: She renamed it herself. Every sign. Marker pen. Still in the good hat.

cards.text: Draft law: in a heatwave, ties are banned. Doug is wearing three. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Ban ties.
right.reaction: Doug wept. He's drawn a tie on his shirt. In biro. It's very neat.

left.label: No. Ties stay.
left.reaction: Doug's tie melted. It was polyester. It's part of the shirt now.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. It's so hot the road's gone soft. Reginald is stuck in it. So is a bus. So is Chad's car. Hose down the road?

right.label: Yes. Cool it down.
right.reaction: The road has set. With Reginald in it. He's fine. He's a landmark.

left.label: No. Wait for dark.
left.reaction: By nightfall the bus had moved four feet. Reginald overtook it.

cards.text: (Reginald is set into the road like a jewel. He looks content. The council wants to dig him out.) Dig him out?

right.label: Yes. Carefully.
right.reaction: Out and safe. He walked straight back in. He likes it there.

left.label: No. He's happy.
left.reaction: He's a roundabout now. Traffic goes round him. Very respectfully.

cards.text: Mayor. My car is still stuck in your road. It's a limited edition. Limited to one. Pay to tow it?

right.label: Yes. Tow it.
right.reaction: Towed. A slice of road came with it. Chad owns it now. He's charging rent.

left.label: No. It's art now.
left.reaction: 'Car in Road'. People love it. Chad is furious. He's on the plinth.

cards.text: Big Carl's paddling pool finally opens today. Gerald is waddling at the ribbon, face first. Cut it before he does!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: A clean cut. Carl blew his whistle in triumph. Then at everyone.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: He cut it with his face. Then got in the pool. He won't get out.

cards.text: Reginald's new crossing opens today. Gerald wants to cut the ribbon. With his face. Get there first!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Cut. Reginald has started across. Expected arrival: Thursday.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it, then stood on the crossing. Reginald is going round him. Slowly.

cards.text: The new snack bar opens today. Gerald is racing to the ribbon, beak first. Snip it before he does!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Open. First customer: Gary. He's just standing there. Humming.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: He cut it, then ate every snack. He's been offered a sponsorship.

cards.text: The wedding arch for Gerald's big day needs opening. Gerald is the groom. He still wants to cut it. Beat the groom!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: You cut it. The swan pedalo was moved to tears. Probably condensation.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: The groom cut his own ribbon. With his face. The pedalo seemed impressed.

cards.text: Gary the vending machine has a new button. Press B4 and he dispenses a free campaign badge. Everyone is pressing B4. Unplug him?

right.label: Yes. Unplug him.
right.reaction: Unplugged. He's still dispensing. Nobody knows how.

left.label: No. Free badges!
left.reaction: Half the town wears a GARY badge. The other half is pressing B4.

cards.text: Mayor, Gary's been unplugged a full day and he's still humming. The power company says he's not on the grid. Investigate?

right.label: Yes. Open him up.
right.reaction: Inside: one crisp, a raffle ticket and a tiny note: 'VOTE GARY'.

left.label: No. Let him hum.
left.reaction: He hummed all night. It's quite soothing. The town slept better.

cards.text: Boss, I've got forty Gary badges. In the coat. Not saying I've switched sides. Saying I've got forty. Confiscate them?

right.label: Yes. Hand them over.
right.reaction: He handed over thirty-nine. He's keeping one. 'For the memories.'

left.label: No. Keep them.
left.reaction: Randy's wearing all forty. He clinks when he walks. He seems torn.

cards.text: Mayor. Gary's been handing out free crisps outside the school. Crisps from 1987. Shut him down?

right.label: Yes. Shut him.
right.reaction: Shut. The children are devastated. The crisps were 'vintage'.

left.label: No. Try one.
left.reaction: It tasted of 1987. Of hope. You nearly voted Gary.

cards.text: (Gary's display flickers: 'DEBATE?'. He's challenging you. Live. On the Bugle's website.) Accept?

right.label: Yes. Debate him.
right.reaction: He answered every question with 'ITEM UNAVAILABLE'. He won. Comfortably.

left.label: No. I don't debate snacks.
left.reaction: Tomorrow's Bugle: 'MAYOR SCARED OF SNACK MACHINE'.

cards.text: (Gary the vending machine owes four years of electricity. He's offered to pay. In crisps. He's already dispensing them.) Accept the crisps?

right.label: Yes. Crisps it is.
right.reaction: The treasury is now 40% crisps. Doug is eating the evidence.

left.label: No. Cash only.
left.reaction: He paid £4.20. In 5p coins. Every coin he's ever been given.

cards.text: Mayor, Gary is polling ahead of you. People say he's 'always there for them'. He is. He's bolted down. Respond?

right.label: Yes. Always be there.
right.reaction: Your desk is on the high street now. You're always there. It's raining.

left.label: No. Let him have it.
left.reaction: GARY SURGES. You are now also behind a fridge.

cards.text: (Gary's display reads 'SORRY'. He has dispensed you a flower made of crisp packets. It's oddly beautiful.) Accept it?

right.label: Yes. Thank you, Gary.
right.reaction: It's in a vase on your desk. Gary hummed a happy hum.

left.label: No. I'm allergic.
left.reaction: His display reads ':(' and then 'OUT OF ORDER'. He's sulking.

cards.text: (Gary's coin slot is glowing. A sign reads 'INSERT MAYOR'. Randy points out that, side on, you are quite coin-shaped.) Climb in and fix him?

right.label: Yes. Climb in.
right.reaction: Something went 'clunk'. You are now item B4.

left.label: No. Absolutely not.
left.reaction: You kept your distance. Gary dispensed a sad crisp. At you.

cards.text: Boss, Gary's dropping out. He'll endorse you by printing your face on every crisp packet. Accept?

right.label: Yes. Crisp face.
right.reaction: Your face is on ten thousand packets. Salt and vinegar. You look worried on all of them.

left.label: No. Dignity.
left.reaction: He's used Randy's face instead. Randy is thrilled.

cards.text: Mayor, Gary has a manifesto. One line: 'FREE SNACKS FOREVER'. People love it. Steal the idea?

right.label: Yes. Free snacks.
right.reaction: Free snacks forever. Doug asked how long forever is. You said 'Tuesday'.

left.label: No. Snacks aren't policy.
left.reaction: 'MAYOR AGAINST SNACKS'. Pages one, two and four.

cards.text: (Election night. Gary's lights blink in a friendly pattern. He's offering you the last packet of 1987 crisps.) Open them?

right.label: Yes. Open them.
right.reaction: They taste of 1987 and of friendship. Gary hummed all night.

left.label: No. Frame them.
left.reaction: They're in the museum: 'Gary's Gift'. He visits every day. On a trolley.

cards.text: (Election night. The queue round Gary isn't for snacks. It's for votes. He's offering you a job: his deputy.) Accept?

right.label: Yes. Deputy to Gary.
right.reaction: He dispensed a chain of office. It's a lanyard. It's yours now.

left.label: No. Fight on.
left.reaction: You stood next to him all night. He's very cold. You're very tired.

cards.text: Mayor, I bought a giant magnifying glass to cool City Hall down. Doug says magnifying glasses set things on fire. Point it at City Hall?

right.label: Yes. Cool us down.
right.reaction: It does not cool things down.

left.label: No. Point it away.
left.reaction: He pointed it at his own pool. It boiled. He's calling it a spa.

cards.text: Big Carl. It's 38 degrees. I've filled the council chamber with water. For safety. Meeting's in ten minutes. Drain it first?

right.label: Yes. Drain it.
right.reaction: Drained. Carl wept. He'd fitted a diving board.

left.label: No. We'll manage.
left.reaction: The meeting went ahead. Underwater. You signed something with a snorkel.

cards.text: Mayor. My ice cream is in the electricity substation. Nora says melting ice cream plus electricity means a town-wide blackout. Leave it in?

right.label: Yes. Leave it.
right.reaction: The ice cream melted the substation. The substation melted the ice cream.

left.label: No. Move it now.
left.reaction: Moved to the library freezer. Linda is shushing it.

cards.text: Boss. The cousins want to cool off in the town's drinking-water reservoir. Four hundred of them. Ban them from the reservoir?

right.label: Yes. Ban them.
right.reaction: Banned. They're in a paddling pool. All four hundred. It's mostly raccoon now.

left.label: No. Quick dip.
left.reaction: Four hundred raccoons. One reservoir. The whole town's water tastes of coat.

cards.text: (Gary the vending machine is overheating. His display reads 'PLEASE DO NOT KICK'. Randy says the trick is to kick him. On camera.) Kick him?

right.label: Yes. Give him a kick.
right.reaction: You kicked your opponent. On camera. He dispensed a sad crisp.

left.label: No. Let him cool.
left.reaction: He cooled down. He dispensed a cold drink. For you. A thank you.

cards.text: (Gerald's wedding. The vicar asks if anyone objects. Barb whispers: 'Object and four hundred geese will riot.') Say nothing?

right.label: Yes. Say nothing.
right.reaction: You held your peace. Gerald nodded at you. The cake was delicious.

left.label: No. I object.
left.reaction: The whole wedding turned round. The pedalo burst into tears.

cards.text: Mayor, I'm swimming UP the ninety-foot waterfall. Big Carl says nobody has ever survived going down it. Swim it with me? Or hold my hat?

right.label: Yes. I'll swim it.
right.reaction: Bev made it up the waterfall. You went down it. Quite a long way down.

left.label: No. I'll hold the hat.
left.reaction: You held the hat. She made it. She waved from the top. You waved the hat.

cards.text: Big Carl. It's so hot the fountain has evaporated. I'm guarding an empty fountain. Still counts. Right?

right.label: Yes. Still counts.
right.reaction: He's guarding it with total commitment. Children are paddling in his shadow.

left.label: No. Take a break.
left.reaction: He took a break. In the fountain. It's empty. He's lying in it. Very relaxed.

cards.text: Big Carl. Refilling the fountain costs £400 in water. I'll fill it myself. With a bucket. Let me?

right.label: Yes. Bucket by bucket.
right.reaction: It took nine hours. It's full. It evaporated at teatime. He's starting again.

left.label: No. Pay for water.
left.reaction: Paid. Full fountain. Carl has rescued four people. None of them were in it.

cards.text: (Councillor Pebbles has found the only shade in town. It's under your desk. He won't come out. He's chewing your shoe.) Leave him?

right.label: Yes. Leave him.
right.reaction: He's stayed all week. The council meets under the desk now. It's cosy.

left.label: No. Out you get.
left.reaction: He's out. He's taken the shoe. You're working barefoot. It's very hot.

cards.text: (Pebbles has invited the rest of the council under your desk. There are seven of them. And Gerald.) Hold the meeting there?

right.label: Yes. Under the desk.
right.reaction: Best meeting ever. Nobody could stand up. Every motion passed.

left.label: No. Everyone out.
left.reaction: Everyone's out. Pebbles has eaten the desk. Problem solved, he says.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot says it's too hot to teach. He'd like school to happen at night. In the freezer aisle at the supermarket.) Allow?

right.label: Yes. Freezer school.
right.reaction: Lessons in the freezer aisle. Attendance is 100%. Everyone's very awake.

left.label: No. Open the windows.
left.reaction: Windows open. Every pigeon in town has enrolled. Hoot is teaching them.

cards.text: Mayor. My restaurant's freezer has broken. In a heatwave. Can I store the fish in the town hall? Just the fish. And the tyres.

right.label: Yes. Store the fish.
right.reaction: Your office smells of haddock. And rubber. Sal says it's a 'rich bouquet'.

left.label: No. Buy ice.
left.reaction: Sal has bought ice. From Gary. In crisp packets. It's melting very fast.

cards.text: Mayor, I've strapped a fan to my scooter. For the heat. It goes faster now. Much faster. I'm on the ring road. Is that okay?

right.label: Yes. Cool off, Bev.
right.reaction: She's lapped the town four times. Coolest person in Bad Town. In every sense.

left.label: No. Slow down.
left.reaction: She's slowed down. To sixty. The fan is pointing at Barb. Barb is grateful.

cards.text: Mayor, the library's air conditioning is the only one working. Four hundred people are here. Nobody's reading. Can I make them read?

right.label: Yes. Make them read.
right.reaction: Everyone's reading. In silence. Very cool. Very well-read town by Friday.

left.label: No. Let them chill.
left.reaction: Let them chill. Somebody's started a disco in Biography.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald would like the fountain reserved for geese during the heatwave. Only geese. He's drawn a sign. It's a goose.) Approve?

right.label: Yes. Geese only.
right.reaction: Geese only. Gerald patrols it. He's let Big Carl in. As a goose.

left.label: No. Share it.
left.reaction: Shared. Gerald honks at every child. Every child honks back. It's a standoff.

cards.text: (Gary the vending machine has overheated. He's dispensing soup. Hot soup. In a heatwave.) Unplug him for the day?

right.label: Yes. Rest, Gary.
right.reaction: Unplugged. He's sulking in the dark. Soup is still coming out. Slowly.

left.label: No. Soup's soup.
left.reaction: Forty people bought soup in 34 degrees. They're sweating. And loyal.

cards.text: Sal. Gary's back on. He's giving out free ice. As an apology. It's ruining my ice trade. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Free ice.
right.reaction: Queues round the block. Sal is selling ice to Gary's queue. Somehow.

left.label: No. Charge for it.
left.reaction: Gary charges 10p. Then gives you the 10p back. He doesn't understand money.

cards.text: Mayor, the whole soup queue has fainted. Gently. The PTA would like Gary moved into the shade. Move him?

right.label: Yes. Shade for Gary.
right.reaction: Four men carried Gary under Toby. Toby seems honoured. Gary is chilled.

left.label: No. He stays.
left.reaction: The queue is back. Fainting in shifts. Very organised.

cards.text: (Gary has fallen in love with the new fridge at the fish shop. He's dispensing notes to it. Every hour.) Arrange a date?

right.label: Yes. Set up a date.
right.reaction: They stood side by side all evening, humming. Sal cried into the haddock.

left.label: No. He's a machine.
left.reaction: Gary has dispensed one sad can, labelled 'for her'. Nobody can open it.

cards.text: (Reginald the tortoise has stopped in the middle of Main Street. It's 35 degrees. He's decided to wait for autumn.) Build him a shade?

right.label: Yes. A little shade.
right.reaction: A parasol over Reginald. Traffic goes round. He's never looked so smug.

left.label: No. Move him.
left.reaction: Barb moved him. He moved back. It took him all day, but he moved back.

cards.text: Mayor! The Reginald parasol is a tourist attraction. I'd like to sell tickets. And hats. Reginald hats. Can I?

right.label: Yes. Sell the hats.
right.reaction: Four hundred Reginald hats sold. Shaped like a shell. Very hot.

left.label: No. He's not a ride.
left.reaction: Chad is selling 'unofficial' hats from a van. They're slightly worse.

cards.text: Mayor. Reginald has now been 'moved' eleven times. He always comes back. Can I give him a parking ticket?

right.label: Yes. Ticket him.
right.reaction: He's ignored it. He's sitting on it. The Bugle calls it 'protest art'.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: Barb is drafting a law: 'No Tortoises on Main Street'. It's 40 pages.

cards.text: (Reginald has reached the other side of Main Street. It took nine days. The town has gathered.) Hold a ceremony?

right.label: Yes. A ceremony.
right.reaction: Brass band, bunting, a speech. Reginald blinked once. It was enough.

left.label: No. It's a road.
left.reaction: He's turned round. He's going back. See you in nine days.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull has stolen every chip on the seafront. All of them. In one swoop. It was beautiful.) Send someone after her?

right.label: Yes. Get the chips.
right.reaction: Big Carl gave chase. Lorraine circled. Carl got a chip. He's keeping it.

left.label: No. Respect her.
left.reaction: The Bugle ran it: 'GULL OF THE YEAR'. Lorraine has framed it. In her nest.

cards.text: Mayor. The seagulls are organised now. They have a leader. It's Lorraine. They want one chip per gull, per day. Deal?

right.label: Yes. Chip tax.
right.reaction: Peace on the seafront. Sal pays in chips. Lorraine collects personally.

left.label: No deals with gulls.
left.reaction: The gulls have taken a pier. They've put up a flag. It's a chip.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull wants a front-page interview. She has 'a lot to say about chips'. She's brought a chip as a press pass.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Let her speak.
right.reaction: She screeched for an hour. Marge printed it all. Best-selling issue this year.

left.label: No. She's a gull.
left.reaction: Lorraine has taken the Bugle's sandwich instead. Marge calls it 'censorship'.

cards.text: (Lorraine has landed on your desk with a single chip. She puts it down. She looks at you. It's a peace offering.) Take it?

right.label: Yes. Eat the chip.
right.reaction: You ate it. She nodded. You're friends now. She will never leave you alone.

left.label: No. Give it back.
left.reaction: She's offended. She's taken your pen. And your stapler. And your lunch.

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. Everyone's coming to City Hall to stand near me. I'm cold, you see. Ghosts are. Can I charge a fee?

right.label: Yes. Charge for cold.
right.reaction: Two pounds a shiver. The treasury is up. Wendy is very proud.

left.label: No. Free chills.
left.reaction: City Hall is packed with sweaty people sighing with relief. Wendy loves the company.

cards.text: Wooo. My chill business is going so well I've hired two more ghosts. From the next town. On zero wages. Is that allowed?

right.label: Yes. Ghost staff.
right.reaction: Three ghosts. Very cold office. Very low costs. Barb has questions.

left.label: No. Pay the ghosts.
left.reaction: You're paying three ghosts. In what, nobody knows. Doug is leaving coins out.

cards.text: Mayor. Four hundred people are standing in the council chamber 'near Wendy'. That's a fire risk. Clear them?

right.label: Yes. Clear the room.
right.reaction: Cleared. They're queuing outside now. In the heat. Glaring.

left.label: No. Let them cool.
left.reaction: The meeting happened anyway. 400 people voted. They all voted for shade.

cards.text: Wooo. The heatwave's ending, Mayor. Nobody needs me now. I'm not sad. I'm a ghost. We're always a bit sad. Say thank you?

right.label: Yes. Thank you, Wendy.
right.reaction: A town-wide thank you. Wendy flickered every light in town. Happily.

left.label: No. Back to haunting.
left.reaction: She's haunting the ice cream van now. It plays its tune backwards.

cards.text: Linda. The time capsule is still knocking. Louder. In Morse. I've translated: 'OPEN ME OR I OPEN MYSELF'. Dig it up now?

right.label: Yes. Dig it up.
right.reaction: Dug up. The geese charged for moving. In bread. Inside: a cassette, a cheese and a letter.

left.label: No. Let it try.
left.reaction: It opened itself. A cassette, a slice of cheese and a letter crawled onto your desk.

cards.text: Boss. I'm judging. I've put everyone through. All forty acts. Including a bin. And a man who was just passing. Is that allowed?

right.label: Yes. Everyone wins.
right.reaction: Forty winners. Forty trophies. The trophies are bins. Everyone's thrilled. Nobody's sure why.

left.label: No. Pick one winner.
left.reaction: He picked the bin. The bin has a record deal. Randy is its manager.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. You banned Bad Town Bucks. So I've bought them all. For acorns. I now own your currency. Want it back?

right.label: Yes. Buy them back.
right.reaction: It cost four hundred acorns. Doug went foraging. He's very good at it.

left.label: No. Keep them.
left.reaction: The squirrels line their nests with them. Very cosy. Very inflationary.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. I'm back. Thank you. But the rooster's still on the roof. Crowing the forecast. People check it before me. Can I evict it?

right.label: Yes. Evict the rooster.
right.reaction: It's on the bakery now. Still right. Steve forecasts it 'sulking'.

left.label: No. Share the weather.
left.reaction: Rooster does mornings. Steve does evenings. Both are wrong on Tuesdays.

cards.text: Linda. Since you evicted the owl, borrowing is up. But every returned book has 'hoo' written inside. Every one. Investigate?

right.label: Yes. Investigate.
right.reaction: It's the owl. It has a library card. Under 'Mr O. Wl'. Linda let it through.

left.label: No. Hoo cares.
left.reaction: The town has decided 'hoo' is a review. Five hoos is the top score.

cards.text: Boss. Clive's been outside your door all week. People think he's the queue. There's a queue behind him now. Forty people. Let them in?

right.label: Yes. Open the door.
right.reaction: Forty people, one cone. You saw them all. Clive went last. Said nothing. Very productive.

left.label: No. Keep it shut.
left.reaction: The queue is still there. They've brought sandwiches. Clive hasn't moved. He's winning.

cards.text: Your stapler has gone missing anyway. A trail of crumbs leads up the clock tower. Something up there is cooing smugly. Send someone up?

right.label: Yes. Send Carl up.
right.reaction: Carl came down with the stapler. And a pigeon that won't let go. It's on your desk now.

left.label: No. Buy a new one.
left.reaction: New stapler. By lunch it was gone. The tower coos louder.

cards.text: Mayor. You moved the second cone. Every morning it's back next to Clive. Nobody moves it. Can I chain it up?

right.label: Yes. Chain it.
right.reaction: Chained. In the morning the chain was next to Clive. Neatly coiled.

left.label: No. Let them be.
left.reaction: The two cones stand together again. People have started leaving flowers.

cards.text: (Councillor Pebbles is still filibustering. Day two. He's eaten the agenda, the minutes and a chair. He's eyeing your shoes.) Concede the turnip?

right.label: Yes. The turnip passes.
right.reaction: The turnip passed. Pebbles ate it. Motion complete.

left.label: No. Hold out.
left.reaction: He ate your shoes. Both. You chaired the rest in socks. Mismatched.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. I'm still holding 9,000 thank-you cards. On the roof. They're getting heavy. And soggy. Deliver them now?

right.label: Yes. Deliver now.
right.reaction: Delivered. A bit soggy. People sent thank-you cards for the thank-you cards.

left.label: No. Hold on.
left.reaction: He's held them so long he's built a nest. Out of cards. He's sitting on it.

cards.text: Wooo. Derek's moved in properly. He's put up shelves. In my wall. He says 'boo', then sorry. Can he be a ghost officially?

right.label: Yes. Ghost Derek.
right.reaction: Derek has a certificate. He's framed it. He apologises to it.

left.label: No. He's a man.
left.reaction: Derek has taken his sheet off. He's just Derek now. People still say 'boo' to him.

cards.text: Big Carl. I've guarded every puddle myself. All night. In flippers. I'm tired. Can I have one helper? Just one. A small one?

right.label: Yes. One helper.
right.reaction: His helper is Timmy. Timmy has a whistle. Carl is terrified of him.

left.label: No. Rest instead.
left.reaction: Carl rested. In a puddle. Guarding it. In his sleep.

cards.text: (Lorraine's Lost Property is on your roof now. She's holding your car keys. She'd like one chip. Per key.) Pay the chips?

right.label: Yes. Chips for keys.
right.reaction: Four keys, four chips. She threw in your car. You don't ask how.

left.label: No. Get a ladder.
left.reaction: Carl climbed up. Lorraine took his whistle. Carl came down. You walk now.

cards.text: (Since you said no to mice, Professor Hoot sulks at lunch. He sits on the dinner trolley. Glaring. Service is very slow.) Give him his own menu?

right.label: Yes. Hoot's menu.
right.reaction: His menu: 'one mouse, optional'. Nobody orders it. He's thrilled anyway.

left.label: No. Same as everyone.
left.reaction: He ate the jelly. All of it. With great dignity.

cards.text: (Trevor is still on your phone. He's started pressing buttons. He has rung the next town's mayor. Twice.) Take your phone back?

right.label: Yes. Phone back.
right.reaction: Trevor has moved to your laptop. He's typed a single word. 'Light'.

left.label: No. Let him talk.
left.reaction: Trevor and the next town's mayor talk every night. He says nothing. They're best friends.

cards.text: (Toby wasn't allowed in the marathon. He's started his own race. It's one tree long. He's in the lead.) Give him a medal anyway?

right.label: Yes. Medal for Toby.
right.reaction: A wooden medal. He wears it on a branch. He's never looked taller.

left.label: No. Rules are rules.
left.reaction: He's dropped an acorn on each of the race committee. Precisely.

objectives.text: Help Gary up when he falls

low:people.title: Melted by the Mob
low:people.text: It was too hot to riot properly, so the town sat outside your office fanning itself angrily until you left. Took ten minutes.

low:business.title: Gone to the Beach
low:business.text: Every shop shut and hung a sign on you: GONE TO THE BEACH. You had not gone to the beach. You were carried there.

low:law.title: Arrested in Shorts
low:law.text: Barb arrested you in her summer uniform: shorts and mirrored glasses. She read you your rights from inside the ice cream van.

low:press.title: Sun-Bleached
low:press.text: The Bugle left your photo in the window all week, in the sun. You've faded. Nobody remembers what you look like. Neither do you.

low:treasury.title: Spent on Ice
low:treasury.text: The whole budget went on ice. The ice melted. Doug is sitting in the puddle that used to be the treasury. It's warm.

high:people.title: Made an Ice Cream Flavour
high:people.text: The town loves you so much Sal named an ice cream after you. Mint and regret. It outsells you. It's mayor now.

high:business.title: Air-Conditioned
high:business.text: Chad loves you so much he installed you in his air-conditioned lobby. As a feature. Visitors are invited to look at you.

high:law.title: Lifeguard for Life
high:law.text: Barb rates you so highly she put you on permanent lifeguard duty with Big Carl. There is no pool. You both watch it.

high:press.title: Too Hot to Print
high:press.text: The Bugle ran you on every page until the presses overheated. The building is a sauna now. Marge interviews you there daily.

rare:dispensed.title: Dispensed
rare:dispensed.text: You went into Gary to fix him. You are now item B4, 85p. You've been bought four times. Each time, you came back.

rare:gary_mayor.title: Deputy to a Vending Machine
rare:gary_mayor.text: Gary is mayor. You are his deputy. Randy is your deputy. Nobody has had a snack since.

trap:magnifier.title: Lightly Toasted
trap:magnifier.text: Magnifying glasses do not cool things down. City Hall is golden brown. So are you. The town voted for someone less crispy.

trap:flooded_council.title: Drowned in Procedure
trap:flooded_council.text: The meeting went ahead underwater. You signed your resignation with a snorkel by mistake. Big Carl rescued the minutes. Not you.

trap:blackout.title: The Great Melt
trap:blackout.text: The ice cream melted the substation. The whole town went dark for a week. The Bugle printed by candlelight: 'YOUR FAULT'. Fair.

trap:reservoir.title: Raccoon Water
trap:reservoir.text: Four hundred raccoons in the reservoir. Every tap in town tastes of coat. Nobody will drink to your health ever again.

trap:kicked_gary.title: Kicked a Candidate
trap:kicked_gary.text: You kicked your opponent on camera. He dispensed one sad crisp. The town will never forgive you. Gary already has.

trap:objected.title: The Objection
trap:objected.text: You objected at a goose wedding. The pedalo cried. Gerald honked for an hour. The guests voted you out from the pews.

trap:waterfall.title: Down the Waterfall
trap:waterfall.text: Bev swam up it. You went down it. A long way down. You washed up in the next county. They made you mayor there instead.

outw:people.title: Too Hot to Vote For
outw:people.text: It was thirty-eight degrees. Nobody could be bothered to vote for anyone. One person voted. It was Bev. She voted for the fan.

outw:business.title: Melted Out of Office
outw:business.text: Every shop shut for the heat. The only business still open was Gary, so Gary was elected by his customers: everyone.

outw:law.title: Arrested for Glistening
outw:law.text: Barb arrested you for 'excessive glistening in a public office'. It's a real law. Doug wrote it in 1987. During a heatwave.

outw:press.title: Puddle Mayor
outw:press.text: The Bugle printed that you'd melted. You hadn't. But the photo was very convincing. You are officially a puddle now.

cliffhangers: Tomorrow: a tortoise is two feet from the kerb.
Tomorrow: something under the pond is knocking.
Tomorrow: your opponent is out of order.
Tomorrow: Bad Town's Got Talent. Nine acts are Bev.
Tomorrow: a goose is in love.
Tomorrow, the last day: Bev has bought a swimming hat.
